notes: Same access route/method as bs25/cl25 (direct HTTP, Demandware SSR HTML, no block). The main-nav item literally labelled 'New Arrivals' points to /c/new-and-trending/, but that page's own H1 and breadcrumb self-link both read 'New & Trending' (not 'New Arrivals') and its SSR grid reports 2,854 Items - far more than the sum of the genuine per-department 'New X' listings below (est. ~1,088), and the same URL's mega-menu flyout has a clearly separate 'Trending' section (Halloween, Harry Potter, Pizza Shop, Cat Shop, Sardine Shop, Rifle Paper Co. x Loloi, etc: themed micro-shops, confirmed via child page /c/new-and-trending/trending/, H1 'Trending Home Decor & Furniture', 1,332 items) that is not about recency at all. So the /c/new-and-trending/ combined listing appears to commingle genuine new-arrival stock with unrelated seasonal/thematic trending collections rather than purely representing 'recently added to the catalogue' - recorded below per the brief's ambiguous-Collection-page instruction rather than silently included or excluded. The reliable New Arrivals signal is the site's own per-department 'new-<dept>' category pages (nav mega-menu 'New Arrivals' flyout lists 9 of them; sitemap_8-category.xml revealed 3 more not linked in the header nav: New Bath, New Clothing & Jewelry, New Outdoor - all fetched directly and confirmed as real, unambiguous product grids with H1s like 'New Furniture', 'New Bath', etc.). Also included New Christmas Decor & Arrivals (/c/holidays/christmas-shop/new-christmas/, 273 items) - same 'new-<dept>' naming/structure pattern, H1 literally contains 'Arrivals'. A parallel christmas-best-sellers-style stale sitemap entry was not an issue here (this one resolved 200 OK, confirmed via curl). Every qty is the PLP's own SSR 'N Items' grid header. No local-language search needed (US/English site); site search itself not queried directly (robots-disallowed for all crawlers, and nav+sitemap already gave complete, unambiguous coverage of this concept).
